issues.description: The problem UML (and textual requirements) define Animal with two attributes (name: String and age: int) and a constructor Animal(String, int) plus getters/setters for the attributes. The solution's Animal.java only defines a single attribute (name) and a constructor Animal(String) with no age field or corresponding getter/setter. Subclasses in the solution (Seal, Pig, Goat) call super(name) and thus follow the solution's constructor, but that contradicts the problem statement's specified Animal constructor and attributes. This mismatch between the specification and the solution (constructor signature and missing attribute) is structural and can confuse students about the required Animal API and how to implement subclasses.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the specification: modify Animal to include private int age; change constructor to public Animal(String name, int age); add getAge() and setAge(int) methods (and keep getName/setName). Update all subclasses' constructors to accept (String name, int age) and call super(name, age). Alternatively, if the intended design is to have only name, update the problem statement/UML to remove the age attribute and the Animal(String,int) constructor so the specification matches the implementation.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Animal with an 'age' attribute and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the template usage and the solution implementation use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). The solution's Animal class only has a constructor Animal(String) and no 'age' field. This mismatch between the problem/UML and the template/solution creates confusion about the expected Animal API and which attributes constructors should initialize.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to show a single-argument constructor Animal(String) and remove the 'age' attribute, or (B) update the template and solution to implement the 'age' field and a two-argument constructor Animal(String, int) with corresponding getter/setter for age. Aligning these names/signatures will remove student confusion about the expected attributes and constructor.
